message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can check the current air quality in Los Angeles on sites like **AirNow.gov** or the **EPA’s Air Quality Index (AQI)** page. Those sites give up‑to‑minute readings for major cities, including Los Angeles, and show whether the air is “Good,” “Moderate,” “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups,” etc.

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also use the **AirVisual** app or the **BreezoMeter** website, which pull data from local monitoring stations and satellite observations.

In general, Los Angeles tends to have a moderate to unhealthy AQI during late spring and summer, especially on hot, dry days when ozone builds up. In winter, traffic and industrial emissions can push the AQI into the “Unhealthy” range on some days. If you’re planning outdoor activities, it’s a good idea to check the AQI forecast for the day and wear a mask if the index is high.
